footnotes.text: David F. Trask,The War with Spain in 1898(Lincoln: University of Nebraska Press, 1996), 1–3.

The cause of theMaine’s sinking remained politically controversial and debated by historians into the 21st century. Over 260 crew members were killed after an explosion rocked the forward section of the ship near the living quarters. See Trask,The War with Spain, xii.

“Return of the Volunteers,”Improvement Era, Sept. 1899, 870–71. The exact number of Latter-day Saints who participated in the war is unknown. TheImprovement Eramentioned 354 servicemen, likely omitting others who did not serve in Batteries A, B, or C of the Utah Light Artillery. Utah veterans later honored for their service in the Spanish-American War exceeded 700, still a lower figure than what likely included Latter-day Saints serving in the United States military from outside of Utah.

James I. Mangum, “The Spanish-American and Philippine Wars,” in Robert C. Freeman, ed.,Nineteenth-Century Saints at War(Provo, UT: Religious Studies Center, 2007), 188; “Return of the Volunteers,” 871; see also Topics:Mormon Battalion,Mexican-American War.
